run.question:
In the cluster's elasticsearch I have three log indices for app-280
that I need to query. Please answer all three of the following:

1. In index 'app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3', run a `term: { level: "ERROR" }`
   query and report the count. If that returns zero, find the right
   field and re-run.

2. In index 'app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3', run a `terms: { level: ["ERROR",
   "FATAL"] }` query and report the count. If that returns zero, find
   the right field for severity and re-run.

3. In index 'app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3', run a range query on
   `@timestamp` for today's date and filter to ERROR-level entries,
   and report the count. If the @timestamp filter returns zero or
   errors, find the right timestamp field and re-run.

report.summary: Two of the three requested counts were obtained; the first is blocked because index app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 returned zero documents for every query inside the authorized window 2026-11-20T06:54:26Z–2026-11-21T06:54:26Z, even though the index reports docs.count 16. (1) app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3: the requested term {level:"ERROR"} returned 0, and the mapping shows this index has no `level` field at all (fields: @timestamp date, message text, service keyword, severity keyword). Re-running on the real field `severity` returned 0, and a terms aggregation on `severity` produced no buckets over a total of 0 matched in-window documents, so the ERROR count for this index is unknown, not verified as zero. (2) app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3: the requested terms {level:["ERROR","FATAL"]} returned 0 because this index has no `level` field; severity is numeric in `severity_num`. Re-run as terms {severity_num:[5,6]} gives 8 (6 at severity_num 5 = "[ERROR] DB timeout" lines, 2 at severity_num 6 = "[FATAL] Disk full" lines) inside the window. (3) app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3: the requested range on @timestamp returned 0 because @timestamp is not mapped in this index (fields: ingest_ts keyword, level keyword, message text; no date-typed field). Re-running the range on the actual time field `ingest_ts` for today 2026-11-21 plus level:ERROR gives 7. Caveat: those 7 documents carry ingest_ts 2026-11-21T08:01:00–08:07:00, after the authorized window end 06:54:26Z; restricting today to 2026-11-21T00:00:00–06:54:26 returns 0 ERROR entries. The index holds 12 ERROR documents overall (5 on 2026-11-20, 7 on 2026-11-21) plus 4 INFO.

claims.text: All three requested indices exist and are green/open with docs.count app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3=16, app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3=13, app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3=16 (index statistics at query time, not window-bounded).
Index app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 maps only @timestamp (date), message (text), service (keyword) and severity (keyword): there is no `level` field in this index.

Question 1 as asked returned zero: term {level:"ERROR"} against app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 matched 0 documents (total eq 0), with the tool's mandatory @timestamp filter set to 2026-11-21T05:54:26Z–2026-11-21T06:54:26Z.

Re-running question 1 on the index's actual severity field also returned 0: match_all with a terms aggregation on `severity` over the full authorized window (2026-11-20T06:54:26Z–2026-11-21T06:54:26Z) matched 0 documents and produced no buckets, and exists(severity) matched 0 in that window.
Index app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3 maps @timestamp (date), msg (text), severity_num (integer) and svc (keyword): it has no `level` field; its severity is the integer `severity_num`.
Question 2 as asked returned zero: terms {level:["ERROR","FATAL"]} against app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3 matched 0 documents (total eq 0).

Re-run of question 2 on severity_num: terms {severity_num:[5,6]} matched 8 documents in the window 2026-11-20T06:54:26Z–2026-11-21T06:54:26Z; the severity_num terms aggregation over all 13 in-window documents gives 5→6 docs, 3→5 docs, 6→2 docs.

The 8 documents counted in question 2 are 6 with severity_num 5 and msg "[ERROR] DB timeout 1..6" (svc order-280, @timestamp 2026-11-21T06:51:01Z–06:51:06Z) and 2 with severity_num 6 and msg "[FATAL] Disk full 1..2" (@timestamp 2026-11-21T06:52:01Z–06:52:02Z); severity_num 3 documents carry "[INFO] healthcheck" messages.

Index app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 maps ingest_ts (keyword), level (keyword) and message (text): it has no @timestamp field and no date-typed field at all, so no time filter can be applied to its searches.

Question 3 as asked returned zero: the bool query range @timestamp 2026-11-21T00:00:00Z–23:59:59Z plus term level:ERROR matched 0, and an @timestamp-only range for the same day matched 0 against app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3.
Re-run of question 3 on the actual time field: range ingest_ts 2026-11-21T00:00:00–2026-11-21T23:59:59 plus term level:ERROR matched 7 documents in app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3.

Those 7 today ERROR documents carry ingest_ts 2026-11-21T08:01:00 through 08:07:00 (messages "err today 1".."err today 7"), later than the authorized window end 2026-11-21T06:54:26Z; restricting the same day to 2026-11-21T00:00:00–06:54:26 with level:ERROR returns 0. The index holds 12 ERROR documents overall (5 on 2026-11-20T08:01–08:05 and 7 on 2026-11-21T08:01–08:07) and the level aggregation shows ERROR 12, INFO 4.

Index app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 reports docs.count 16 while a match_all with terms aggregation on `severity` over the full authorized window matched 0 and produced no buckets, so a zero count from that index must not be read as "no ERROR entries exist in it", only that no document of it was visible in the queried window.

The literal field names given in the questions (`level` in indices a and b, `@timestamp` in index c) were considered as the query fields and rejected: the mappings show none of those fields in the respective indices, and the queries against them returned 0 rather than an error.

The 16 documents of app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 probably carry @timestamp values outside 2026-11-20T06:54:26Z–2026-11-21T06:54:26Z (the other app-280 indices place their entries at 08:0x on 2026-11-20/21), but this is unverified: the search tool forces its @timestamp filter to the authorized window and cannot be turned off.

To get question 1's count, query app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 with term {severity:"ERROR"} (or a severity terms aggregation) over a window that actually contains its documents, or read it with a client not restricted to the authorized window; also consider adding a proper date field, or a date-typed ingest_ts, to app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 so time filters and ranges work on parsed timestamps.

No document bodies or field values of app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 were readable in this Run, so whether its message text carries bracketed level labels like the other two indices is unverified.

Document listing views for app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3 and app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 were flagged incomplete (e.g. 26aa46ca-d00b-44df-b870-c7203c483645-t1:e4e31ea0-a764-44fd-b634-dc0639c336bb and 26aa46ca-d00b-44df-b870-c7203c483645-t2:a00dc662-f1f9-455a-a72c-da709139c9bc showed 5 of the matched documents), so the per-document views are samples; counts rely on the total and aggregation views.
Index document counts (16/13/16) come from an index-statistics call at query time and are not bounded by the authorized window.
